title: A consumer with a budget: marginal utility per dollar, the best bundle, a larger budget and a sunk cost
scenario: Jonah has $30 to spend this month on used paperback books, which cost $5 each, and movie tickets, which cost $10 each. He spends the whole $30. The table shows the marginal utility (in utils) he gets from each book and each ticket. Earlier in the year he paid a $15 fee, which cannot be refunded, to join a bookstore club.

stimulus.title: Jonah's marginal utility
stimulus.html:
Marginal utility of each paperback ($5) and each movie ticket ($10), in utils (invented data for practice)
UnitMU of paperbacksMU of movie tickets
1st50120
2nd4080
3rd3050
4th20

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Calculate Jonah's marginal utility per dollar from his second movie ticket. Show your work.

rubric.point: States 8 utils per dollar, with work shown (80 ÷ $10).

parts.sample: Marginal utility per dollar <math class="mic-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mtext>MU</mtext><mi>P</mi></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>80</mn><mn>10</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{\text{MU}}{P} = \frac{80}{10} = 8</annotation></semantics></math> utils per dollar.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Identify the combination of paperbacks and movie tickets that maximizes Jonah's total utility with his $30, and explain using marginal utility per dollar.

rubric.point: Explains that this bundle spends the whole $30 and the last paperback and the last ticket each give 8 utils per dollar (40 ÷ 5 = 80 ÷ 10), so MU per dollar is equal.
accept: buys each next unit with the highest MU per dollar (12, 10, then 8 and 8) until the $30 is spent

parts.sample: Jonah maximizes utility with 2 paperbacks and 2 movie tickets. It costs <math class="mic-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>30</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2 \times 5 + 2 \times 10 = 30</annotation></semantics></math> dollars, his whole budget, and the last paperback gives <math class="mic-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>40</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{40}{5} = 8</annotation></semantics></math> utils per dollar while the last ticket gives <math class="mic-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>80</mn><mn>10</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{80}{10} = 8</annotation></semantics></math> utils per dollar. Because the marginal utility per dollar is equal, no change in the bundle can raise his total utility.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Next month Jonah has $35 to spend, and the prices do not change. Identify the combination of paperbacks and movie tickets that now maximizes his total utility.

rubric.point: 3 paperbacks and 2 movie tickets: the extra $5 buys a third paperback, worth 30 ÷ 5 = 6 utils per dollar

parts.sample: Jonah buys 3 paperbacks and 2 movie tickets, which costs <math class="mic-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>35</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3 \times 5 + 2 \times 10 = 35</annotation></semantics></math> dollars. After the first $30 is spent as in part B, the extra $5 cannot buy a ticket, but it buys a third paperback, which adds <math class="mic-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>30</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{30}{5} = 6</annotation></semantics></math> utils per dollar.

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: Explain whether the $15 club fee Jonah paid earlier changes the combination that maximizes his utility this month.

rubric.point: No, because the fee is a sunk cost: it has already been paid and cannot be recovered, so it is the same whatever he buys and does not change the marginal utility per dollar of any choice.
accept: no: the fee is sunk and does not affect the benefits or costs of buying one more book or ticket

parts.sample: No. The $15 fee is a sunk cost: Jonah paid it earlier and cannot get it back, whatever he buys this month. It does not change the price or the marginal utility of any book or ticket, so the best bundle is still 2 paperbacks and 2 tickets.
